name: Louder Wind Flutes
description: The wind flutes that play in fog once you have found a Wind Flute (every 60 to 89 seconds of the game's clock while the fog lasts: Flute1 with 1 to 4 flutes found, Flute3 with 5 to 9, Flute5 with 10 to 12) are made louder, so they are heard clearly over the music. How much louder is the Louder Wind Flutes slider in the patcher window: 2 to 100 times (a whole number, 5 unless you move it; type it in the box beside the slider too). The game's own flute recordings are much quieter than its music, and the game already plays them at full volume, so the sounds themselves are made louder as the game loads them. They never distort: the loudest moments are held just under the loudest a sound can be, so from about 3 times up the quiet parts gain the most and every higher number is still louder. At 5 times, with the game's Sound and Music sliders at their maximum, the flutes are a little louder than the loudest song and clearly louder than the others. Every other sound, the music, the Sound and Music sliders and when the flutes play are unchanged; the game's sound files are never changed. **On by default.** **Needs no other patch.** **Works the same with every other patch and in every population mode.** **Not yet heard in a running game** (checked with the game's own sound library and by emulation of the stock executable). The companion is "VVFP VV4 Louder Flutes.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll, and the slider's number is written beside it in "VVFP VV4 Louder Flutes.txt"; saves are never written by it.
behavior_changes: The sound loader's call of FSOUND_Sample_Load (0x40C4E1 in 0x40C490, every sound effect the game loads) goes to the companion, which makes the same call; when the file is Flute1.ogg, Flute3.ogg or Flute5.ogg and FMOD made a 16-bit signed PCM sample, it locks the whole sample (FSOUND_Sample_Lock), makes it N times louder and unlocks it, N the slider (2 to 100, 5 by default) read at start from "VVFP VV4 Louder Flutes.txt" beside the companion (above 100 is 100, below 2 is 2, none is 5). The gain goes through a limiter worked out over the whole sample first: each frame's largest gain that keeps it at or under -1 dBFS (29,204), falling ahead of a loud frame by at most 3 dB per 220 frames and recovering after it by at most 3 dB per 4,410 frames (24-bit fixed point). Nothing is clipped.

Measured with both sliders at their maximum (the louder half's RMS; the loudest song -12.9 dBFS): stock -22.9 / -26.5 / -25.5 dBFS (Flute1 / 3 / 5); x 2 -16.8 / -20.5 / -19.5; x 5 -9.9 / -12.6 / -11.7; x 10 -7.4 / -8.3 / -7.3; x 100 -5.9 / -6.1 / -5.2.
explicit_non_changes: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces the one call at run time, only after verifying its stock bytes; FMOD functions missing from the game's fmod.dll mean nothing is installed.

Every other sound and the music are loaded exactly as before; the volume the game asks for (3.0 x the Sound slider, 0x4AB3A8), when the flutes play (the weather update 0x46BE10) and which flute plays are the game's own. A sample that is not 16-bit signed PCM, or that FMOD does not hand back whole, is left as it is.
The game's sound files are never changed; the companion only reads its setting file and writes nothing to a save, a villager record or a file; no text is shown.
evidence_status: the real fmod.dll 3.74 loads each flute as 16-bit stereo signed PCM (mode 0x151) and hands back the whole sample from FSOUND_Sample_Lock, equal within 1 to a decode of the .ogg (a scratch 32-bit probe, 2026-11-10); the companion's install and its scaling are emulated on the rendered executable in tests/test_vv4_louder_wind_flutes.py; runtime/player confirmation pending

runtime_detours.routine: the sound loader 0x40C490's call of FSOUND_Sample_Load (the thunk 0x47099E) goes to the companion, which makes the same call and makes the three wind flute samples N times louder (the slider), held under clipping
runtime_detours.installed_by: VVFP VV4 Louder Flutes.dll, VvfpStartup (started by VVFP Startup.dll, second word)
